summary.oneLiner: Sai Life Sciences is a leading integrated CRDMO in India benefiting from global pharma's supply chain diversification away from China, with strong execution in discovery, development, and manufacturing. Its strategic capex expansion in peptides, ADCs, and oligonucleotides positions it to capture high-growth next-gen therapeutics demand while improving margins toward 28-30%.

one-line thesis: Sai Life Sciences is a leading integrated CRDMO in India benefiting from global pharma's supply chain diversification away from China, with strong execution in discovery, development, and manufacturing. Its strategic capex expansion in peptides, ADCs, and oligonucleotides positions it to capture high-growth next-gen therapeutics demand while improving margins toward 28-30%.
financial scorecard: rev: +16% YoY; EBITDA: +42% YoY; PAT: +105% YoY; orderbook: strong visibility for FY27; netdebt: reduced via IPO repayment
guidance: Long-term revenue CAGR of 15-20% over 3-5 years; EBITDA margin target of 28-30% within next 2-3 years; ROCE target mid-to-high-teens
order book & pipeline: Strong visibility for FY27 driven by scaling commercial molecules, FTE-to-manufacturing pipeline, and new modality programs; no specific dollar value disclosed
segment / subsidiary detail: CDMO: 63% of revenue; CRO: 37% of revenue; CRO growth driven by pharma clients (now 37-38% of CRO revenue vs 30% last year); discovery chemistry: 60% of CRO; biology/DMPK: 40%; peptide center launched in Hyderabad; new modalities (ADC, oligo) capex underway
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion into peptide conjugates, ADCs, oligonucleotides; potential for end-to-end service integration across discovery to commercial supply; geographic diversification via Boston center; scaling FTE-to-commercial pipeline
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin expanded 458 bps to 25% in FY25; cost optimization and capacity utilization drove margin growth; one-time INR34cr bad debt provision in Q4 impacted margin; long-term target 28-30%
capex / expansion: FY25: INR408cr; FY26 guidance: INR700cr (INR550cr for core capacity, INR50-70cr for new modalities, remainder for visibility-triggered investments); maintenance capex: ~INR70cr
capital allocation: Prioritizing capex for manufacturing and new modalities; debt repayment completed (INR720cr via IPO); future capex funded via internal accruals and debt; no dividends or buybacks mentioned
risks & watch-items: Biotech funding volatility; macro uncertainty from US tariffs/MFN orders; long lead times for commercialization of pipeline molecules; execution risk on large capex projects; customer concentration risk (18 of top 25 pharma)
management quality / tone: Confident, forward-looking, and execution-focused; emphasized supply chain shift as key tailwind; highlighted customer-led innovation in new modalities; downplayed near-term macro noise; reiterated long-term guidance firmly
non-obvious takeaways: The INR34cr Q4 provision was a one-time de-stocking issue with a customer, not systemic credit risk; 37% of CRO revenue now from pharma (not biotech), indicating structural shift; Boston center is EBITDA profitable and contributes $14-15M revenue; capex is largely for FY27 delivery, not FY26

themes.title: Pharma CDMO / CRDMO & API import-substitution
themes.need: Global biopharma's China+1 sourcing plus a peptide/biologics modality boom drive India's CDMO/CRDMO build-out and API import-substitution. ANTHEM/COHANCE/NEULANDLAB/SYNGENE-tier on CRDMO (peptides/ADCs/oligos); DIVISLAB/LAURUSLABS on peptide CDMO; AKUMS/INNOVACAP/RUBICON on formulation CDMO; AARTIPHARM/SUPRIYA/AARTIDRUGS/SOLARA on APIs; SIGACHI/NATCAPSUQ/VIDHIING on excipients.
themes.driver: Customer regulatory filings unlocking dedicated capacity; new CRDMO molecule wins; API price/volume recovery.
